observation.visible_scene: A single yellow, cushion-cut faceted gemstone rests on a smooth reflective surface against a plain light-gray background. A mirror image of the stone appears directly below it. The stone occupies the upper-center of the frame throughout.
visible_changes: Over the excerpt the gemstone's internal facet pattern shifts, indicating a slow rotation of the stone (or of the viewing/lighting angle): a small dark facet located at the right-center in the early frames gradually moves toward the right edge and then disappears, while a bright white highlight grows and migrates across the upper-center table facet, becoming most prominent in the final frames.
The silhouette orientation of the stone changes subtly (tilt of the girdle corners), consistent with the stone turning rather than a pure brightness change.
The reflection below tracks these same facet and highlight changes, confirming it is a reflection of the same object and not a separate stone.
The stone's overall position in the frame stays roughly centered with only minor drift; the gap between the stone and its reflection remains approximately constant.
The background and the reflective surface show no visible motion of their own.
outside_clip_unknowns: What mechanism rotates the stone (turntable, hand, or moving light source) is not shown.
The light source and its position are not visible.
Whether the rotation continues, reverses, or stops after the last frame is unknown.
Any earlier state before the first frame is unknown.
uncertain_details: Because the background is featureless, it cannot be confirmed whether the apparent change is the stone rotating in place or the lighting/viewing angle changing; the changing silhouette favors object rotation but is not definitive.
The exact axis and direction of rotation are hard to pin down from the facet shifts alone.
Any small camera movement (zoom/pan) cannot be distinguished from stone motion given the uniform background.
